subject: General Knowledge
topic: Seven Wonders of the World — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Petra, the rose-red city carved into cliff faces and one of the New Seven Wonders, is located in which country?

options.option_text: Saudi Arabia, in the Arabian Peninsula region
Jordan, the Hashemite Kingdom in western Asia
Egypt, near the ancient Sinai Peninsula border
Turkey, in the Anatolian region of Asia Minor

questions.explanation: Petra lies in the Ma'an Governorate of southern Jordan and was the capital of the ancient Nabataean Kingdom. Saudi Arabia is the most tempting wrong answer because Petra sits close to the Saudi border, but it is firmly within Jordanian territory.

questions.stem: Which of the New Seven Wonders of the World is situated on the Yucatán Peninsula of North America?

options.option_text: Machu Picchu, the Inca citadel high in the Andes
Chichen Itza, the ancient Mayan pyramid in Mexico
Christ the Redeemer, the hilltop statue in Brazil
Petra, the rock-carved ancient city in Jordan

questions.explanation: Chichen Itza is a pre-Columbian Mayan city on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula; its landmark is the El Castillo pyramid (Temple of Kukulcán). Machu Picchu is in Peru, not Mexico — the most frequent wrong pick due to both being Latin American archaeological sites.

questions.stem: The ancient wonder 'Mausoleum at Halicarnassus' — the origin of the English word 'mausoleum' — stood in the territory of which present-day country?

options.option_text: Greece, in the classical region of ancient Attica
Egypt, in the Nile Delta near ancient Alexandria
Turkey, in the Bodrum region of modern Anatolia
Iraq, in ancient Mesopotamia near old Babylon

questions.explanation: Halicarnassus was a Greek city in Caria (southwestern Anatolia), today the city of Bodrum in Turkey. The tomb was built for King Mausolus of Caria (~350 BCE). Greece is the leading distractor because the structure was designed by Greek architects in the Hellenistic style, but its geographic location belongs to modern Turkey.

questions.stem: The 'New Seven Wonders of the World' announced in 2007 were selected via a global public poll organised by which body?

options.option_text: UNESCO, the UN's education, science and culture arm
New Seven Wonders Foundation, a private Swiss entity
United Nations General Assembly based in New York
International Olympic Committee headquartered in Lausanne

questions.explanation: The New Seven Wonders campaign was run by the New Seven Wonders Foundation, a private non-profit organisation founded by Swiss-Canadian filmmaker Bernard Weber. UNESCO publicly distanced itself from the poll and stated it had no involvement — making UNESCO the most dangerous distractor in any exam setting.

questions.stem: Among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, which was a giant bronze statue of the sun god Helios erected at the entrance of a harbour on a Greek island?

options.option_text: Statue of Zeus at Olympia, a seated gold-ivory figure
Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, a grand marble shrine
Colossus of Rhodes, a bronze statue at harbour entry
Lighthouse of Alexandria, a tall beacon tower on Pharos

questions.explanation: The Colossus of Rhodes was a ~33-metre bronze statue of Helios (sun god) guarding the harbour of Rhodes island in the Aegean Sea; it was toppled by an earthquake in 226 BCE. The Lighthouse of Alexandria is a tempting distractor as it was also built on an island, but it was a navigational tower in Egypt, not a harbour-entrance statue.

questions.stem: The ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, was built on which island located just off the Egyptian coast?

options.option_text: Antirhodos, a small island inside Alexandria's royal harbour
Pharos, in the western harbour mouth of Alexandria city
Cyprus, the large island in the eastern Mediterranean Sea
Rhodes, the Greek island in the south Aegean Sea region

questions.explanation: The Lighthouse of Alexandria was constructed on the island of Pharos during the reign of Ptolemy I (~280 BCE) and stood roughly 100–135 metres tall. Rhodes is a craftily placed distractor since the Colossus of Rhodes is itself an ancient wonder; Antirhodos was a real island inside Alexandria's royal harbour but was not the lighthouse's location.

questions.stem: Construction of the Colosseum in Rome — officially called the Flavian Amphitheatre — was begun under which Roman emperor of the Flavian dynasty?

options.option_text: Julius Caesar, the dictator who transformed the republic
Augustus Caesar, the first emperor of the Roman Empire
Vespasian, the founder of the Flavian imperial dynasty
Nero, the emperor during the great fire of Rome in 64 CE

questions.explanation: Construction began under Emperor Vespasian (r. 69–79 CE), founder of the Flavian dynasty — giving the Colosseum its formal name Amphitheatrum Flavium. It was completed by his son Titus in 80 CE. Nero is a well-designed distractor: before Vespasian, Nero's Domus Aurea palace stood on the same site, and Vespasian demolished it to build the Colosseum on the drained ornamental lake.
